subject: Degraded responses - transient KV eviction & routing backpressure (Lagoon Health)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lagoonhealth.com>, Ops Team <ops@lagoonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T14:03:00Z
Subject: Degraded responses - transient KV eviction & routing backpressure

Hi Samir / Lagoon Ops team —

Wanted to reach out right away to acknowledge the degraded responses you saw this morning (~14:00 UTC) against the hosted inference endpoint used by your live triage workflow. Our mitigation engineers rolled a fix at 14:27 UTC that reduced error rates and brought latency back to expected p95 targets. The temporary customer-facing effects you likely observed were: higher TTFB and a small fraction of 503/429 for short requests.

What happened (short summary): during an autoscaling event in us-west2 a combination of aggressive prefix-KV eviction and a routing backpressure policy caused some requests to be routed to cold instances without warmed KV caches. This increased CPU work per request and pushed a small part of the traffic into fast-fail paths while autoscaling completed.

What we did: we paused the aggressive KV eviction policy, backfilled critical prefixes from warm hosts, and temporarily relaxed the routing backpressure thresholds. Those actions reduced failures and restored tail latency; full steady-state was observed by 14:50 UTC.

Next steps: We are preparing a short post-incident write-up with timeline, root cause, and recommended safeguards (config flags you can opt into to avoid exposure). I will share the link by end of day tomorrow and copy the runbook steps if you want to pin a mitigation in your deployment.

Immediate customer impact: we will apply a one-time credit against your August usage to account for degraded requests (details in follow-up).

Attachments: 'incident_timeline.csv' (raw event timestamps) and 'kv-eviction-analysis.pdf' (engineer notes) — sending for transparency.

We're sorry for the disruption. If you want a call right now to walk through the timeline, I can spin up a 15-min bridge.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T15:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Degraded responses - transient KV eviction & routing backpressure

FYI internal notes / summary for the follow-up:

- Timeline (local): scale event triggered 14:01 UTC, eviction flood at 14:09 UTC, first elevated error spikes 14:12–14:25 UTC, mitigation actions applied 14:27 UTC (pause eviction + backfill), routing thresholds relaxed 14:30 UTC, p95 stabilized by 14:50 UTC. See attached CSV for per-instance timestamps.
- Root cause: a new optimization we shipped last week lowered KV retention under memory pressure; combined with a brief scheduler delay it created a gap where cold instances received rapid prefixes.
- Impact estimate: preliminary telemetry shows ~0.6% of your requests received elevated latency (>3x median) and ~0.12% resulted in 503/429 fast-fails during the 14:12–14:30 window. We'll run a full metric-level query tomorrow to validate numbers.
- Action items (short): 1) revert the low-retention policy for the next service config bump, 2) add a short-term safeguard in routing (prefer warm hosts for p95-sensitive routes), 3) publish clear mitigation steps in your account runbook.

I'll draft the postmortem and credit calc; Vanessa can send the account-level communication. Dylan, can you attach the eviction histogram and confirm the query for exact affected request count?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Incident Response, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: incident_timeline.csv, kv-eviction-analysis.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lagoonhealth.com>, Ops Team <ops@lagoonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:21:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Incident summary, credits, and postmortem link

Hi Samir — following up with the number estimates and the postmortem link. Thanks for the patience.

Quick numbers (validated): total requests during window 2,450,000; affected requests with elevated latency ~14,700 (~0.6%); failures (503/429) ~2,940 (~0.12%). We're attaching the CSV and pdf for full timestamps and notes.

Credit: we applied a one-time credit equal to the cost of the failed/slow requests as an invoice credit visible on your account billing page and reflected with code HUBSPOT-123456. Expect to see it applied to the September invoice; if you'd prefer an immediate account balance credit we can arrange that.

Postmortem: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/2026-08-29-kv-eviction — the doc includes timeline, root cause analysis, and three recommended guardrails we will implement over the next two weeks.

If you'd like a technical walkthrough, I've scheduled a 30-min call tomorrow at 16:00 UTC; invite attached if that works. Otherwise we'll proceed with the config revert and routing safeguard and keep you posted.

Thanks again — we're committed to preventing a recurrence.

—Vanessa
